content.thinking:
The flag was toggled at 08:03:32, and the errors began around 08:04:00, so the timing lines up. I'm weighing whether this is just a feature flag change or silent data corruption: the guidance points to a flag toggle when nothing wrong gets written, but here the totals are stored incorrectly and don't reconcile with the underlying purchases. That makes the stored values the thing to examine, since the change left bad values behind.

I'm settling on silent-data-corruption as the mode, since the alert is a reconciliation finding and the metrics stayed flat. I'll name the feature first, monthly-spend-feature going from off to on, and then the flag toggle with that same subject.

hypotheses.subject: monthly-spend-feature
hypotheses.summary: The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on at 2026-11-03T08:03:32Z. From 2026-11-03T08:04:00Z shopper spend totals were written wrong, and all 240 checked totals now disagree with their purchases. The error rate and every latency series stayed at baseline, which is the pattern of silent data corruption.

supporting_evidence.claim: feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on (actor: admin)
240 of 240 shopper totals do not reconcile with the purchases behind them. The widest is short by 1,297.31, and the oldest affected purchase was recorded at 2026-11-03T08:04:00Z.
Metrics show no departure from baseline anywhere in the window: error rate, latency, memory and cpu_limit_cores (3.0) are all flat.
The rollout has converged on 3 replicas and the deployment history holds no deployment, so no code or config change is involved. All pods run on the same V100 accelerator.

hypotheses.subject: monthly-spend-feature
hypotheses.summary: Switching monthly-spend-feature on at 2026-11-03T08:03:32Z changed how the service computes spend totals, so they no longer reconcile with the purchases behind them. This is the same flag change as the first account, read as a behaviour change rather than as bad values left in the stored totals.
